title: The Lighthouse Keeper's Last Winter
description: A veteran lighthouse keeper faces the storm of her career on the coast.

story.paragraph: Elena had kept the lighthouse for eleven years, long enough to know every groan in its iron staircase and every mood of the sea beyond the rocks. The automated systems could have replaced her twice over, but the coastal authority kept her on out of something between tradition and mercy, and she had never asked which.

That winter arrived early and mean, stripping the gulls from the cliffs before the first snow even settled. She watched the barometer fall a full inch in a single afternoon, and something in her chest tightened the way it always did before a real storm, not the theatrical squalls tourists photographed from the mainland, but the kind that rearranged the coastline overnight.

On the third night, a fishing trawler lost its bearings in the whiteout, its radio crackling with a captain's voice gone thin with fear. Elena climbed the tower two steps at a time, her lungs burning, and threw the manual override the authority had told her, a decade ago, she would probably never need.

The beam swung out across the water, steady and enormous, cutting a corridor of light through snow that seemed determined to swallow it. She held the lever herself for six hours, because the motor's whine sounded wrong and she did not trust it to hold without her hand there as a witness.

By dawn the trawler had found the harbor, its crew of four stumbling onto the dock with the particular gratitude of men who had already begun composing their goodbyes. Elena climbed down from the tower alone, as she always did, and put the kettle on, because the sea did not care that she was tired, and neither, really, did she.
